raw_response:
I will do it mostly the way I have done these past years, with a few small adjustments if prices look too high. On my 5 mu, wheat and maize are one after the other, so the full 5 mu goes to wheat first, then the same 5 mu goes to summer maize. I have only 2 people at home, so I will keep things simple and use what is proven around Quzhou. For wheat, I will use an improved seed, put enough base fertilizer so the seedlings stand strong through winter, and then add nitrogen at jointing. Wheat cannot be short of fertilizer, or the heads get small, so I would rather spend a little more than lose grain. I have well water, so I will water wheat about 3 times if the year is normal: once before winter if the soil is dry, once at jointing, and once around grain filling. For maize after wheat, I will plant a hybrid because the yield is steadier and most people around me do the same. Maize eats fertilizer hard, especially nitrogen, so I will not save too much there. I will give some compound fertilizer at sowing and topdress once when it is growing fast. Since summer rain helps, I will usually irrigate maize 1 to 2 times depending on rainfall. For pests, I will not spray blindly, but wheat usually needs 2 sprays in a normal year and maize about 2 as well. On my small area, rotary tillage is enough and saves labor compared with deep ploughing every time.
